title: Ops weekly radar: SRE reliability prep and action list
content:
Purpose and audience
- Quick prep notes for the weekly SRE ops sync (standing Wed 10:00).
- Audience: oncall leads, reliability eng, infra owners, and product incident liaisons.
- Goal: align on SLO drift, paging noise, top-3 ongoing incidents, and 1-2 operational experiments to run this week.

Top-of-mind metrics (quick snapshot for standup)
- Customer-facing SLOs (30d trailing):
  - latencies (p50/p95/p99): 12ms / 78ms / 320ms (hosted API, text gen, avg seq=256) — p95 up 6% week-over-week
  - error rate: 0.71% (5xx + rate-limited) — stable vs prior week but trending to SRE-4821 spike windows
  - availability: 99.91% (monthly rolling) — within SLA but close to threshold for a few prod routes
- Internal SLOs: KV cache hit rate 62% (target 70%) — cache invalidation pattern suspected on model rollouts
- Paging volume: 142 pages last 7 days (normalized to oncall roster), up from 98 last week. Primary sources: autoscaler flaps (41%), model-evictions (28%), transient infra networking (14%), other (17%).

Paging trends + quick hypotheses
- Autoscaler flaps: majority tied to dedicated-region burst behavior between 03:00–06:00 UTC (low traffic) — repeated scale-down then scale-up. Hypothesis: new mem/cpu quotas from infra-agent change (INF-3957) causing incorrect utilization reporting.
- Model-evictions: linked to recent rollout of quantized variant (q4) for 1.3B models — eviction probability increased under sustained long-context requests. Hypothesis: kernel selection path ignored higher KV footprint for certain op sequences.
- Networking blips: intermittent packet loss in us-west-2 host pool; impact mostly small requests but shows up as timeouts in streaming RPC. Ops ticket created.

Top 3 incidents to call out (for review)
1) SRE-4821 (2026-06-20) - Hosted API transient surge -> rate-limiter overflow
   - Symptom: 2min window of elevated 429 and 5xx when external client retried aggressively after perceived timeout.
   - Root cause (current): client-side retry storm + rate-limiter configured with per-route burst bucket not sufficient for multi-tenant spikes.
   - Current status: postmortem draft linked. Remediation in flight: add adaptive per-client token bucket and a global soft-fallback policy.
   - Action needed: sign-off on adaptive token bucket design (owner: Evan) by EOD Fri.
2) INF-3957 (ongoing) - Autoscaler misreporting leading to flaps (investigation)
   - Symptom: repeated scale-down/up cycles in dedicated pools during low traffic; correlated with agent v2.4 push.
   - Hypothesis: agent CPU reporting aggregated incorrectly across containers; triggers scale decision.
   - Next steps: rollback agent delta in one canary cluster, monitor for 24h. (owner: Kai).
3) MODEL-EV-122 (2026-06-23) - Model eviction spike on q4 quantized rollouts
   - Symptom: Elevated evictions and increased tail latency for long-context inference.
   - Investigation: kernel path uses compacted KV layout but neglects per-layer LRU warm-up; presence of long prefix requests causes cache thrash.
   - Mitigation: temporary rollout pause and restore full-precision variant for 2 affected customers.

This week's agenda (10:00 standup, 30 minutes)
- 0:00–0:03 quick snapshot (me)
- 0:03–0:10 Pager trends + SLO anomalies (Evan)
- 0:10–0:18 Incident reviews (owners): SRE-4821, INF-3957, MODEL-EV-122
- 0:18–0:24 Ops experiments / safety nets (discussion):
    - Adaptive token bucket proposal timeline
    - Canary rollback plan for agent v2.4
    - KV cache warm-up simulation (small bench to run mid-day)
- 0:24–0:27 Triage: any new oncall escalations? Immediate mitigations?
- 0:27–0:30 Action item assignment + quick wins

Action items (capture + owners)
- Evan: finalize adaptive token bucket design doc and cost analysis; circulate by 2026-06-27. (linked to SRE-4821)
- Kai: initiate rollback of infra agent v2.4 in canary cluster and report metrics 24h post-rollback; target complete 2026-06-25.
- Jules: run KV warm-up bench (script kv-warmup-v2) against q4 variant on staging and collect eviction traces; deliver short findings by 2026-06-26.
- Samira (me): coordinate customer comms for the two affected accounts for MODEL-EV-122 and draft internal status note; send by EOD 2026-06-24.
- Oncall rotation lead (Nate): tweak pager thresholds to add suppression for autoscaler flaps during known low-traffic windows; proposal for review 2026-06-26.
- Reliability tooling: add SLO drift alert to channel #slo-ops when p95 latency increases >5% week-over-week for two consecutive days (owner: reliability infra).

Open questions / unresolved items
- Is the cache invalidation during rollouts expected for q4 quantized models, or is this an implementation regression? (ask model-runtime team)
- Do we have telemetry to tie client retries to distinct API keys/tenants to better rate-limit noisy customers? (if not, add as infra work)
- What are the expected billing implications of adding per-client adaptive token buckets? Need finance/monetization check.

Notes to self (scratchy)
- Bring up anecdote about the night-time flaps — helpful to show histogram of scale events binned by hour; will prepare a 1-slide graph.
- Bookmark: confluence postmortem SRE-4821 draft (link above) — need to push one concrete rollback step if adaptive bucket rollout will take longer.
- Remind product folks: rate-limiter changes may alter user-facing 429 semantics; coordinate with docs & SDK teams.

Quick-run checklist before standup
- [ ] Upload last 7d paging heatmap (Grafana link)
- [ ] Attach p95 latency trend for hosted-api top routes
- [ ] Confirm rollback slot with infra (Kai)
- [ ] Ping model-runtime lead for brush-up on q4 expected behavior

Post-meeting follow-ups (what I'll update after the sync)
- Update SRE tracker doc with owners + ETA for each action item.
- If adaptive bucket design approved, open infra-implementation ticket and tag security/finance for review.
- Schedule 30m follow-up with model-runtime + serving-runtime to plan KV-cache simulation outcomes and rollout policy change (tentatively 2026-06-29).

Random scratch ideas to explore (later)
- Lightweight simulated client that creates realistic retry storms to test token bucket behavior; could live under /tools/sim/retstorm.
- Add a tiny circuit-breaker in the gateway that detects global retry amplification and returns a 429 with Retry-After for noisy tenants; low-risk experiment.

End-note: keep the sync focused — only deep-dive if an owner requests code-level help. Otherwise track and follow-up offline.
